The '''2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was the 122nd final of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]], the most prestigious provincial [[hurling]] championship. The match, contested by [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]], took place on 14 July 2013 at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]], and started at 4:00 p.m.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://munster.gaa.ie/2013/06/23/munster-senior-hurling-championship-semi-final-cork-v-clare/|title= Cork 0-23 Clare 0-15|date=23 June 2013|work=Munster GAA|access-date=26 June 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0906131754-superb-limerick-unseat-champions-tipperary/ |title=Limerick 1-18 Tipperary 1-15 |date=9 June 2013 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=26 June 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130613015129/http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/0906131754-superb-limerick-unseat-champions-tipperary |archive-date=13 June 2013 }}</ref> It was Limerick's 45th Munster final and Cork's 80th. In Ireland, the match was televised live on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' on [[RTÉ Two]], with commentary from [[Ger Canning]] and [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/2013/06/23/munster-senior-hurling-championship-final-4/ |title=2013 Munster Final Details |date=2013 |work=Munster GAA |access-date=2 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130701235554/http://munster.gaa.ie/2013/06/23/munster-senior-hurling-championship-final-4/ |archive-date=1 July 2013 }}</ref>

The championship winners were awarded a place in the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship semi-finals|semi-finals]] of the [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], while the loser went through to the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship quarter-finals|quarter-finals]].
	
==Route to the final==
===Limerick===

Entering the Munster Championship at the semi-final stage by virtue of a bye, Limerick's first game was at home against [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] on 9 June 2013. Limerick were very much the underdogs going into the game as, it was believed, the burden of playing in Division 1B of the [[National Hurling League]] would ultimately prove their undoing, while Tipperary would exploit time and space to exert unbearable pressure and ultimately restate their credentials as [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]]'s most likely challengers for the All-Ireland. All did not go to plan for the Premier County, who were 0-03 to 0-01 behind early on and were five down when [[Seán Tobin]] scored the opening goal for Limerick after [[Brendan Cummins (Tipperary hurler)|Brendan Cummins]] had scooped the ball clear in a goalmouth scramble. Limerick led by 1-07 to 0-07 at half-time. [[John O'Dwyer]] came off the bench to make his championship debut and scored 1-03 in the second half for Tipp. He fired home a brilliant 49th-minute goal and Tipp led by 1-13 to 1-09. Limerick fought back to draw level at 1-14 apiece and set up a grandstand finish. They edged two points clear with points from subs [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]] and [[Niall Moran]], before [[Eoin Kelly (Tipperary hurler)|Eoin Kelly]] dragged Tipp back into contention with five minutes left. But Limerick were flying and they bagged the final two scores through captain [[Donal O'Grady (Limerick hurler)|Donal O'Grady]] and [[Declan Hannon]] to secure a 1-18 to 1-15 victory, their first over Tipperary since 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-blaze-a-hot-trail-into-munster-final-1.1422216|title=Limerick blaze a hot trail into Munster final|date=9 June 2013|work=Irish Times|access-date=12 July 2013|first=Seán|last=Moran}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-learn-winning-formula-233772.html|title=Limerick learn winning formula|date=10 June 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=12 July 2013|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/super-subs-lead-late-charge-as-treaty-muzzle-tipps-top-dogs-29332388.html|title=Super subs lead late charge as Treaty muzzle Tipp's top dogs|date=10 June 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=12 July 2013|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}</ref>

===Cork===

Also entering the Munster Championship at the semi-final stage by virtue of a bye, Cork's first game was at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] against [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]], quarter-final winners over [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]], on 23 June 2013. Clare were slight favourites as they had won a [[Waterford Crystal Cup]] clash early in the year – before winning the two National League fixtures between the teams, including a relegation play-off. Cork started without injured duo [[Paudie O'Sullivan]] and [[Lorcán McLoughlin]], while team captain [[Pa Cronin]] also started on the bench. Clare played with a strong wind in the opening period and led by 0-11 to 0-08 at half-time. Cork scored the final point of the first half via goalkeeper [[Anthony Nash (hurler)|Anthony Nash]]'s long-range free, before they opened the second half in devastating fashion. Eight points on the bounce ensured that Cork's three-point deficit had become a five-point lead. Cork won the second half by 0-15 to 0-04 to score their first victory over Clare in 2013 – at the fourth attempt.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/clare-blown-away-in-the-second-half-1.1439989|title=Clare blown away in the second half|date=23 June 2013|work=Irish Times|access-date=12 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/corks-young-guns-silence-critics-as-clare-feel-backlash-29367040.html|title=Cork's young guns silence critics as Clare feel backlash|date=24 June 2013|work=Irish Independent|access-date=12 July 2013|first=Vincent|last=Hogan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/clinical-cork-get-wind-in-their-sails-234991.html|title=Clinical Cork get wind in their sails|date=24 June 2013|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=12 July 2013|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

==Pre-match==
Cork were appearing in the Munster final for the 80th time since the championship was founded in 1888. The team had won the Munster final fifty times (most recently in [[2006 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2006]]) and were runners-up twenty-nine times (most recently in [[2010 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2010]]). Limerick were appearing in the provincial showpiece for the 45th time. The team had won the championship eighteen times (most recently in [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1996]]) and were runners-up twenty-six times (most recently in [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2007]]).

Ticket prices for the final started at €20 for the Clare End and City End terraces, and were available at €30 for uncovered stand and €35 for the covered Mackey Stand.

==Match==
===Summary ===
Limerick beat fourteen-man Cork by 0-24 to 0-15 to secure the Munster crown for the first time since [[1996 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|1996]]. The Munster final failed to produce a goal for the first time since [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1978]]. Cork's [[Patrick Horgan]] was sent-off in first half injury time for striking Limerick wing-back [[Paudie O'Brien]] on the helmet under a high ball.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://munster.gaa.ie/2013/07/14/munster-senior-hurling-championship-final-4/|title= Limerick 0-24 Cork 0-15|date=14 July 2013|work=Munster GAA|access-date=24 July 2013 }}</ref>

Limerick took advantage and went on to compile a comfortable victory. The final whistle was greeted by scenes of euphoria at the Limerick city venue, as a seventeen-year wait for Munster glory came to an end. The Munster Cup was lifted by captain [[Donal O'Grady (Limerick hurler)|Donal O'Grady]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/limerick-cork-live-987596-Jul2013/ |title=As it happened: Limerick v Cork, Munster senior hurling final |date=14 July 2013 |work=The Score |access-date=24 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130716141018/http://www.thescore.ie/limerick-cork-live-987596-Jul2013/ |archive-date=16 July 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/news/flashback-2013-munster-shc-final-limerick-v-cork/|title =Flashback: 2013 Munster SHC Final - Limerick v Cork|date=5 June 2020|work=GAA.ie |access-date=9 June 2020}}</ref>

==Reaction==
Limerick manager John Allen believed the element of surprise and a well drilled and disciplined panel of players were the deciding factors in their victory over Cork.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0715/462542-limerick-boss-allen-hails-his-players/|title= Limerick boss John Allen hails his players' spirit and discipline after win over Cork|date=15 July 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=24 July 2013 }}</ref>
Allen, who was in his second year as manager, said he had absolute faith that his players would deliver victory on the big day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/1407131940-allen-delighted-with-significant-victory-/ |title=Allen never doubted Limerick |date=15 July 2013 |work=GAA.ie |access-date=24 July 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130717042737/http://www.gaa.ie/gaa-news-and-videos/daily-news/1/1407131940-allen-delighted-with-significant-victory-/ |archive-date=17 July 2013 }}</ref>
Cork manager Jimmy Barry-Murphy criticised the decision to send off Patrick Horgan in the first half, saying "It was an unbelievable decision that is all I can say, anyone that was at the match can judge for themselves."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thescore.ie/jimmy-barry-murphy-patrick-horgan-sending-off-992997-Jul2013/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130724150956/http://www.thescore.ie/jimmy-barry-murphy-patrick-horgan-sending-off-992997-Jul2013/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 July 2013 |title=Jimmy Barry-Murphy: 'It was an unbelievable decision' |date=15 June 2013 |work=Score.ie |access-date=24 July 2013 }}</ref>
Speaking on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' programme later that night, former Cork goalkeeper [[Donal Óg Cusack]] agreed that the sending off was harsh, saying "I think it was extremely harsh - I don't think the intention was there, I know technically the referee can say he made the right decision but referees are encouraged to use their common sense."<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-sport/what-the-sunday-game-said-of-limerick-s-win-1-5285154|title= What the Sunday Game said of Limerick's win|date=15 July 2013|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=24 July 2013 }}</ref>

Declan Hannon, Richie McCarthy and James Ryan were shortlisted by ''The Sunday Game'' panel for the Man of the Match award before confirming James Ryan as the winner.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0715/462596-ryan-the-best-feeling-i-ever-had-in-my-life/|title= James Ryan credits the fans support for Limerick's long-awaited Munster Hurling title|date=16 July 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=24 July 2013 }}</ref>
